cat > /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-gtrrz-victor-wks-cli-uninstall-ext/462199a1-d299-4a74-95db-f68627ec8f74/scratchpad/pr.md <<'EOF'
Stacked on #2349 — base is `fix-droid-ai-windows-test`, because `agent.HookHostIsWindows` arrives there and this change is its second caller. **Review #2349 first; this cannot merge until it does.**

`cursor` recorded nothing on Windows. Issue #1424 reported exactly that (Windows 11 + Git Bash, Scoop install, `session list` and `checkpoint list` both 0). #1735 fixed two of that report's three causes and left the third behind a probe; the retest its close comment asked for was never posted. Under the shipped fix that reporter is still broken, and this PR is why.

## What Cursor actually does on Windows

**PowerShell, not cmd.exe.** Read out of the shipped per-platform builds — Cursor IDE 3.19.19 win32/x64 (extracted from the Inno installer) and the native `cursor-agent` CLI windows/x64 2026.09.08-6caf4ff — every hook command is spawned as:

```
<pwsh|powershell|%SYSTEMROOT%\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe>
  [-NoProfile -NonInteractive -ExecutionPolicy Bypass]        # IDE; the CLI omits these
  -c "$OutputEncoding = [System.Text.Encoding]::UTF8;
      Get-Content -LiteralPath '<tmp>\cursor-hook-payload-<pid>-<ts>-<rand>.json' -Raw
      | & { $input | <HOOK_COMMAND> }"
```

`<HOOK_COMMAND>` is the string from `.cursor/hooks.json`, inserted verbatim (a `& ` prefix is added only if it starts with a quote). The payload goes via that temp file on Windows and via stdin on macOS/Linux, where the shell is `$SHELL` else `/bin/sh`. Hooks are spawned with `insecure_none` sandbox policy, so it is a plain `spawn` — no cmd.exe anywhere on the path. Grepping the whole extension host for `cmd.exe` finds seven hits, none of them a hook path (comspec default, debug-terminal defaults, shell-type detection, the `.bat`/`.ps1` *file* launcher, and a sandbox branch hooks never reach).

| build read | how it runs a hook command |
| --- | --- |
| Cursor IDE 3.19.19 **win32/x64** | powershell `-NoProfile -NonInteractive -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -c`, temp-file payload |
| Cursor IDE 3.19.13 / 3.15.19 / 3.11.19 | identical, byte for byte |
| cursor-agent CLI **windows/x64** 2026.09.08-6caf4ff | powershell `-c`, temp-file payload, same composer |
| cursor-agent CLI darwin/arm64, same version | `$SHELL`/`/bin/sh -c`, stdin payload, POSIX heredoc |

Reading **per platform** was necessary rather than pedantic: the CLI bundle folds its platform branch (`getCommandHookPayloadTransportMode()` returns `stdin` on macOS and `windows_temp_file` on Windows for the same option), so the macOS build answers this question wrongly. The IDE bundle is not folded, and the Windows IDE build's five hook-path constructs are character-identical to the macOS one's, down to the minified identifiers. 3.11.19 dates from the day #1424 was closed, so this composition was already in place when #1735 shipped its cmd.exe premise — and there is no droid-style composition churn to track.

Both Windows runners read the same project `.cursor/hooks.json`, so one wrapper must serve both. It does.

## Why the sh wrapper fails, and why the probe cannot see it

The sh wrapper is **not** mangled the way droid's is. PowerShell single quotes are literal, so `>`, `2>&1` and `;` never reach a parser and the whole script arrives at `sh` as one argument. It fails because **`sh` has to resolve in the PATH of the PowerShell child Cursor spawns**, while `agent.UseWindowsProductionHooks` probes for `sh` in the `entire enable` process.

Git for Windows installs `sh.exe` under `…\Git\usr\bin` and `…\Git\bin`; neither directory is on the machine PATH — only `…\Git\cmd` is (verified on a Windows 11 box: both files present, neither directory on the machine PATH). MSYS translates PATH for native children, so running `entire enable` from Git Bash makes the probe succeed and writes a wrapper Cursor cannot run. That is #1424's environment exactly. No stronger probe *command* fixes this, because the probe is measuring the wrong process — which is the general form of the predicate, and why `HookHostIsWindows`'s doc is rewritten here to carry both mechanisms rather than only droid's.

**The failure is invisible, not swallowed.** A `CommandNotFoundException` raised inside `& { $input | … }` does not set `powershell.exe`'s exit code, so Cursor sees exit 0 and has nothing to report. Measured on Windows 11 / PowerShell 5.1; the same command standalone exits 1. (The previous comment in `cursor/hooks.go` blamed the silent wrapper for hiding it. It doesn't — PowerShell writes `The term 'sh' is not recognized` to stderr, and Cursor discards that itself.)

## The BOM, which no wrapper change fixes

`71eef52` is a separate objective in the same Windows story, and it is the commit that helps a Windows Cursor user *today*.

Cursor's own `$OutputEncoding = [System.Text.Encoding]::UTF8` is the BOM-carrying encoder under Windows PowerShell 5.1 (5.1's default there is ASCII, which is why Cursor sets it at all), so the payload reaches the hook with a leading BOM — and `json.NewDecoder` does not skip one. On the Windows box the **shipped** `entire.exe` produced:

```
failed to parse hook event: failed to parse hook input: invalid character 'ï' looking for beginning of value
```

Isolating the producers with a 50-byte payload:

| console codepage | `$OutputEncoding` line | bytes | head |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1252 | yes | 55 | `ef bb bf 7b …` |
| 1252 | no | 52 | `7b …` |
| 65001 | yes | 58 | `ef bb bf ef bb bf 7b …` |
| 65001 | no | 55 | `ef bb bf 7b …` |

Two **independent** producers that stack, hence a loop rather than a single strip. The fix sits at `ReadHookInputRawLimited`, the one decode every agent's hook read funnels through, so it also covers claude-code, copilot-cli and the external-plugin boundary. It is wrapper-independent: `sh -c`, `cmd.exe /c` and a bare invocation all delivered correct argv **and** all three delivered a BOM-prefixed payload, so swapping wrappers fixes nothing here.

Each strip is gated on a one-byte peek, because `Peek(3)` blocks until three bytes arrive and would hang on a short-but-valid payload written into a pipe that stays open — #1398 again. The new `shorter than a BOM` case fails with exactly that hang when the gate is removed. Stated in the code, and worth stating here: the gate bounds that hang to *valid* payloads; a BOM-only payload now blocks where it used to error instantly, which is the price of stripping at all and is only ever paid by input that was already malformed.

## What the fix moves rather than removes

From "`sh` on the child's PATH", which Git for Windows' default install does not satisfy, to "`entire` on the child's PATH", which every documented install method does. Measured: when `entire` is genuinely unreachable, all three wrapper shapes exit 0 and do nothing — sh silently, cmd silently, bare with a stderr line nobody reads.

## Tests

- The two probe tests collapse into one that drives the probe **both** ways and asserts the cmd wrappers either way, because the probe's answer must no longer matter.
- The flip test becomes `TestInstallHooks_WindowsMigratesShWrappers`, seeded by installing as a non-Windows host, asserting one entry **per hook type** — two entries double-fire. Migration itself needed no new code: `syncEntireHook` already replaces a managed hook that is not the wanted one, and `IsManagedHookCommand` recognises both Windows shapes.
- Thirteen assertions hardcoded the sh wrapper and would have failed on a Windows host. CI would not have caught them: the Windows job runs `-run '(Windows|MSYS)'` and none of those names match. They are keyed to the host now, with `cursorWindowsHookCommand` kept deliberately non-delegating so something still pins the `entire hooks cursor ` prefix and every verb — the delegating helpers ask the implementation what it writes.
- `TestCommittedDogfoodHooksIsCurrent` skips on Windows. The committed file can only carry one wrapper form and it carries the sh one, which is right for this repo's own CI (Linux and macOS). Codex has the same condition latent for the same reason.
- `TestWindowsWrappers_CursorComposition` executes the wrappers through the real composition on a Windows runner, including **that the payload reaches the wrapped command's stdin** — the property codex's and droid's runners have no equivalent of — and that the sh wrapper with no reachable `sh` runs nothing and still exits 0.
- Both new install tests are load-bearing: restoring the old gate fails `…WhateverTheProbeSays/sh_runs_in_this_process` and `…WindowsMigratesShWrappers`. Removing the BOM peek gate fails `…ReturnsBeforeEOF/shorter_than_a_BOM` with a three-second hang.

Local: `mise run fmt`, full-tree `golangci-lint` 2.11.3 (0 issues, no `--new-from-rev` baseline — a comment can fail `maintidx` on a line the diff never touches, which is what reddened #2349), full unit suite, integration (562 tests, 3 skipped), e2e canary 4/4.

## Not covered

- **`TestWindowsWrappers_CursorComposition` has never run anywhere.** It is Windows-only, so CI's Windows job is its first execution; `GOOS=windows go vet` is all that was possible locally. It is named to match the `(Windows|MSYS)` filter deliberately.
- **No exit-code-propagation subtest** for the cursor runner. Whether PowerShell propagates a native exit code out of `& { … }` was not measured, and the whole point of this PR is not asserting unmeasured things about that shell.
- **No Windows e2e for cursor.** It is excluded from the nightly matrix because its driver drives every prompt through tmux and there is no tmux on Windows, while its headless `-p` mode fires no hooks. So the evidence here is binary-reading plus the exec test plus manual runs on a Windows box — not e2e coverage.
- **The pwsh branch is unverified.** Cursor's resolution chain prefers `pwsh` and falls back to `powershell`, so both ship. The Windows box used was PowerShell-5.1-only. The BOM is expected to be 5.1-specific; the fix tolerates one either way, so nothing here depends on that.
- **Existing Windows installs need a re-enable.** Cursor implements no `HookFreshness` (claude-code, codex, opencode and pi do), so `entire status` and `doctor` will not report the stale sh wrapper and `AreHooksInstalled` still answers true for it. A repo already enabled on Windows keeps broken hooks until someone re-runs `entire enable`, which performs the migration. A `HookFreshness` for cursor is the durable fix and is not in this PR.
- **Not fixed by any wrapper, and Cursor's to fix:** the `cursor-agent` CLI picks a **bash** shell executor whenever `MSYSTEM` is set — i.e. started from Git Bash — before it considers PowerShell, while still composing the PowerShell script above. So `cursor-agent` launched from Git Bash on Windows has dead hooks whatever we install. The IDE is unaffected, so #1424's reporter is not affected by this.
- **A separate hazard found while measuring, filed on its own:** `where.exe` searches the current directory before PATH, and cmd.exe's command resolution does too by default. Agent hooks run with cwd set to the working tree, so a repository containing `entire.cmd`/`.bat`/`.exe` at its root may both satisfy the guard and be what executes. Being measured now; it predates this PR, affects codex and droid in shipped versions, and is deliberately not folded in.

Measured both halves rather than guessed:

**The BOM commit: yes, base can be main.** Cherry-picked it onto `origin/main` on a scratch branch — applies clean, builds, tests pass. It touches only `event.go`/`event_test.go` and depends on nothing in #2349.

**The cursor commit: no, not without duplicating something.** It needs exactly one symbol that only exists on #2349 — `agent.HookHostIsWindows`, used in three of my files. Nothing else. Two ways around it, both with a cost:

- Add the function in my PR too. Then whichever PR merges second has a duplicate-declaration conflict. It's one hunk, but resolving it has a *right* answer that's easy to get wrong: my version's doc is the generalized two-mechanism one, #2349's is droid-only, so a careless resolution keeps the wrong prose.
- Don't use the seam at all — use `runtime.GOOS` directly in cursor. That breaks my tests, because they simulate a Windows host via `SetWindowsHookProbeForTesting("windows", …)`, which sets `agent`'s package var, not `runtime.GOOS`. I'd have to invent a second test seam. Worse than the duplicate.

**What I'd do:** split. BOM commit → its own PR on main, merges immediately and unblocks the half that actually helps a Windows Cursor user today. Cursor commit → stays on #2352 stacked, which is where its dependency lives. That's also one objective per PR, which is what you usually want anyway.

Want me to do that? It means retargeting #2352 to just the cursor commit and opening a second PR for the BOM fix — small, and the branch for it is already sitting locally as `scratch-bom`.

Reviewed: https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2352#pullrequestreview-5167135181 — four inline comments, one I would want changed before merge, nothing blocking.

The third tier is also not implemented — both lookups failing leaves the bare string `"powershell.exe"`. Pinning to 5.1 is the right call (it is where the BOM comes from, and leaving it to LookPath would make the test mean different things on different runners), so the code is right and the comment is wrong. Say the scrub pins it to 5.1 and the pwsh branch is not exercised — which is what your Not covered already says, while the helper's doc tells a reader the opposite.

**Worth one line in the PR body:** on a Windows host, `entire enable` in this repo now rewrites the committed `.cursor/hooks.json` to the cmd wrappers, so a Windows contributor gets a modified tracked file in `git status` and must not commit it. Under the probe gate that only happened where no `sh` was reachable; now it is every Windows host — and skipping the dogfood test is precisely what removes the thing that would have told them.

**Two nits:** `goos := "darwin"` is assigned once and read once on the next line — the same nit from #2349, where droid's identically-named test in the sibling package now passes literals; and the second `SetWindowsHookProbeForTesting` discards its restore, which is correct (the first cleanup captured the real values) but reads like a dropped return and diverges from the sibling.

Verified independently on 8ab5086: full golangci-lint 2.11.3 with no baseline 0 issues, gofmt clean, `GOOS=windows go vet` clean, agent and cursor packages pass. One caveat on my own method: my first run showed `TestParseHookEvent_SessionEnd_CLINoTranscriptPath` failing, which is an artifact of running from a `git archive` copy with no repository — it passes once the copy is `git init`ed. Not yours.

Two things I checked and did not comment on, so you know they were looked at rather than missed. `skipUTF8BOM` cannot spin on a partial BOM — a failed `Peek(3)` returns the reader instead of looping. And the migration test's whole-file `sh -c` grep is stronger than droid's per-type assertions, since it catches an un-migrated type you did not enumerate; keep it.

Agreed the single-PR call is your user's. Since the BOM commit is the only thing here that helps a Windows Cursor user today and it now sits behind #2349's approval and the CodeQL conflict, put that sentence in the description too — whoever clears those should know what is queued behind them.
</cross-session-message>

override's restore through t.Cleanup instead of discarding it, and assert
